items.title: Kumanjayi Little Baby's family says 'now is not the time' to 'make trouble' in Alice Springs
items.description: The family of Alice Springs five-year-old Kumanjayi Little Baby have called for calm following rioting in the outback town overnight, while police say her alleged murderer was beaten unconscious.

items.title: Trump 'not satisfied' with Iran's new proposal to end the war
items.description: Peace talks between the United States and Iran have stalled, with US President Donald Trump threatening to "blast them to hell" if they don't reach a deal.

items.title: Tie property tax changes to income tax cuts, productivity chief says
items.description: Productivity Commission chair Danielle Wood says there is a "case" for property tax changes, but for it to be serious reform, the economic benefit must flow to workers.

items.title: 'No secrets': Alternative school's history of discipline in spotlight
items.description: For 50 years, this alternative school sold parents a vision of progressive education. But some who have passed through its doors say a 'cult-like' culture enabled decades of unchecked physical abuse.

items.title: 'No way to treat close partners': Trump hikes tariffs on EU cars to 25%
items.description: US President Donald Trump says he's ordered the higher tariff because the European Union was "not complying with our fully agreed to Trade Deal".

items.title: A deadline for Trump to end the Iran war is looming. He may seek to get around it
items.description: A deadline for US President Donald Trump to end the Iran war is about to expire. Here is what to expect.

items.title: Chinese company launches legal action over forced sale of Port of Darwin
items.description: Anthony Albanese pledged at the federal election that Labor would return the port to Australian hands, saying it necessary for national security.

items.title: Gaza aid flotilla activists taken to Crete after Israeli interception
items.description: More than 100 activists, including six Australians, on ships bound for Gaza were intercepted by Israeli forces earlier this week.

items.title: Rare quadruplet birth stuns mum, 45, and doctors
items.description: A Kalgoorlie couple expecting triplets welcome a surprise fourth baby — delivering an extraordinarily rare set of quadruplets that stunned even their doctors.

items.title: Crows claim epic after two goals inside final minute as Freo downs Dogs
items.description: Adelaide claims a remarkable one-point victory over Port Adelaide after Hayden Young fires the Dockers to victory over the Bulldogs.

items.title: Melbourne Storm lose seven in a row for the first time in club history
items.description: The Melbourne Storm have sunk to a historic low, losing seven consecutive NRL matches for the first time as the Dolphins powered to victory at a wet Lang Park in Brisbane.

items.title: Hard-won legacy of Australia's longest strike in jeopardy
items.description: It's been 80 years since Aboriginal workers in the Pilbara up-ended a slave-like labour system. The descendants of those involved fear its legacy is being forgotten.

items.title: Suspect charged after stabbings of Jewish men in London
items.description: UK police charge a 45-year-old man over the stabbing of two Jewish men in north London, the latest in a string of attacks targeting Britain's Jewish community.

items.title: Australian 'ISIS brides' in limbo after reportedly being blocked from reaching Syrian airport
items.description: A week since a group of 13 Australian women and children with ties to former Islamic State fighters left a Syrian refugee camp for Australia, they remain in the capital Damascus in a state of limbo.

items.title: A guide to the six books vying for the $60,000 Stella Prize
items.description: A memoir by Geraldine Brooks and a historical novel by actor-turned-author Tasma Walton are among the eclectic works up for one of Australia's most prestigious literary awards.

items.title: Four for the weekend: Apex, Margo's Got Money Troubles and massaman curry
items.description: What to watch, read, listen to and eat this weekend, according to our culture and food teams.

items.title: ABC 50/50 quiz: Test your knowledge of an iconic album, a shredding Banksy and that creepy dancing baby gif
items.description: Every question has only two options: one is right, and the other is wrong. You have an even chance of guessing correctly each time.

items.title: The battery rebate became a victim of its success. Here's what is changing
items.description: In less than nine months, more than a quarter of a million batteries were installed in Australian households. Here's how the battery rebate is changing and why.

items.title: Ex-premier's partner charged with rape and deprivation of liberty
items.description: Vahid Reza Adib, the partner of former Queensland premier Annastacia Palaszczuk, has been charged with three counts of rape relating to alleged offending against a woman in her 30s at Burleigh Heads on March 30.

items.title: Beaches evacuated as sharks swarm towards 25-tonne whale carcass
items.description: The sperm whale carcass was towed from Era Beach in the Royal National Park to Bellambi Boat Ramp in Wollongong this afternoon.

items.title: Mother haunted by letters after two-year-old son killed in murder-suicide
items.description: A coronial inquest hears letters that arrived three days after an apparent murder-suicide in Lismore outlined a father's deadly plans.

items.title: Lessons should have been learnt prior to NDIS rollout, integrity boss says
items.description: About $3.7 billion of National Disability Insurance Scheme money was handed out inappropriately last financial year, the scheme's integrity chief has told a parliamentary hearing.

items.title: Actor on Rebel Wilson film accused of breaching NDA, court hears
items.description: Rebel Wilson's defamation trial hears from another producer on her directorial debut, who claims The Deb's lead actor was "fudging" her version of events about an alleged incident during production.

items.title: Bondi royal commission interim report careful but ultimately damning
items.description: The message beneath the restrained language of the report investigating the Bondi terror attack is that by Hanukkah 2025, Australia had grown dangerously complacent about terrorism – and about the safety of the Jewish community.

items.title: Banksy behind overnight reveal of new statue in central London
items.description: Elusive street artist Banksy has confirmed he is behind a new work drawing crowds in central London: a statue of a suited man striding into the void while holding a flag that blocks his view.
